newsitem.title: ZAIRE: War's impact spreads within Zaire - aid worker.
newsitem.headline: War's impact spreads within Zaire - aid worker.

text.p: An aid worker said on Friday that eastern Zaire's multi-sided war was having an impact on wide stretches of country as many frightened villagers fled to the bush.
Andrew Hunt of Christian Aid told Reuters that he flew over much of eastern Zaire this week and saw semi-deserted villages and normally busy roads now empty.
He also said that thousands of people had fled westwards from the conflict and were reported to be short of food.
Hunt visited the town of Lubutu, about 400 km (250 miles) northwest of Bukavu, scene of fierce battles late last month, and met a student, one of about 50 fugitives there from the fighting.

The student, who hitched a ride to Lubutu on a stolen aid vehicle, said several thousand people with ankles swollen from walking and empty stomachs were concentrated in the town of Hombo 90 km (55 miles) west of Bukavu.
"He said that he personally had not eaten for three days and he thought the situation was similar for the other people," said Hunt, Christian Aid programme officer for Zaire's South Kivu province.
Hunt flew over the country east of Lubutu following the tarred road as far as Walikale.
"The villages were pretty empty and we saw no markets whatsoever along the whole 200 km (120 mile) stretch between Lubutu and Walikale," he said.
He said of the people: "They have just decided to go into the bush for a few days because of the general insecurity."
Action for Churches Together (ACT) told a meeting on Nairobi on Friday that an aerial survey this week had revealed a large concentration of people in the jungle between Hombo and Walikale.
ACT said the mixture of Rwandan refugees and displaced Zaireans had survived in the jungle for about three weeks and were in very bad condition. It said they were very tense and robbing each other.
Hunt said there was quite a lot of food in the Lubutu area -- rice and palm oil -- because it was harvest time but the town was still tense.
"There is a general fear that the conflict is going to spread that far west," he said.
He also flew to Bunia, about 550 km (340 miles) north of the Zairean city of Goma which is on the border with Uganda.
He said he found the region very tense and in fear of a rebel attack.
"The repercussions of the conflict in Kivu are stretching fairly wide," he said.
